title: GPX Bounding Box Tool: Track Extents in Degrees
description: Extract the south, west, north and east bounds of a GPX file with the GPX Bounding Box Tool — min/max coordinates from every point. Free, local.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-point park loop spanning latitudes 40.7681 to 40.7740 and longitudes −73.9719 to −73.9630 has its box read off the extremes — no map required.
quick_answer: The GPX Bounding Box Tool reads every point in a GPX file and reports the south, west, north and east extremes — the smallest axis-aligned box containing the whole recording. Load the file in your browser and read the four numbers that APIs, map fits and spatial queries ask for.
steps_intro: Four extremes from every point in the file:

body.t: A web map needs an extent to frame the track. The box is that extent — feed it to your map library's fitBounds and the track fills the screen.

A folder of GPX files becomes searchable by region once each file's box is catalogued — the metadata a track library is built on.
A box suddenly spanning two continents means one corrupted point teleported. The extremes make the bad point findable.

Points between 40.7681–40.7740 latitude and −73.9719–−73.9630 longitude give the box directly. Note the longitude span (0.0089°) looks bigger than the latitude span (0.0059°) while covering similar ground — degrees shrink east-west, as this site never tires of repeating.

examples.label: Example · The box is not the route

body.t: An L-shaped hike's box includes the whole corner the route never visits. Boxes contain; they do not describe — for shape, the track itself (or its length from the route-stats tools) is the document.
